newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish grain harvest put at 24 mln Tonnes, imports seen up.
newsitem.headline: Polish grain harvest put at 24 mln Tonnes, imports seen up.

text.p: Poland's grain harvest in 1996 is likely to be around 24.0 million tonnes, which will increase the country's imports next year, the agriculture minister said on Wednesday.
"We will have about 24 million tonnes of grain...which means Poland would have to import more than 1.5 million," Roman Jagielinski told a news conference.

A ministry report released at the conference estimated Poland's import needs at between 1.3 and 1.7 million tonnes in the 1996/97 growing season (July/June), after the country bought abroad 1.8 million in 1995/96.

Poland's food market regulator, the Agriculture Market Agency (ARR), on Wednesday downgraded its harvest estimate to 24.0-24.5 million tonnes from 24.2-25.2, which the Central Statistical Office (GUS) set as the benchmark in September.
The government-run ARR earlier said it would likely import grain at the end of the second quarter of 1997 if it was forced to intervene on Polish grain markets next year.
Jagielinski said that to facilitate needed grain imports Poland extended its zero-duty on imported grain for another six month period ending on July 31, 1997.
"The council of ministers has suspended duty on grain imports unitl the end of July 1997," Jagielinski said.

In a seperate report issued by GUS on Wednesday, it maintained the September harvest estimate, adding that Poland's 1996 wheat output should ease nearly one percent to 8.6 million tonnes and rye output fall 8.8 percent to 5.7 million tonnes.
GUS said Poland's barley output should increase by 4.8 percent to 3.4 million tonnes in 1996, while the country's oat output should rise by 4.9 percent to 1.6 million tonnes.
The ministry's report said rapeseed purchases by Poland's edible oil refineries since the 1996 harvest shrunk to 335,000 tonnes from 1.1 million tonnes in the same period of last year.
It said Poland imported some 127,500 tonnes of rapeseed since this year's harvest. GUS estimates put Poland's 1996 rapeseed output at 438,000 tonnes, down from 1.38 million last year.
The ministry said Poland's white sugar output should rise to some two million tonnes this year, up 27 percent from 1995.

Jagielinski said sugar not absorbed by the domestic market next year or exported with a subsidy in line with international trade agreements was likely to be bought by the government to rebuild the country's reserves.
